logo_override.validation_detail: webfetch returned 'Image fetched successfully', confirming HTTP 200 plus a real image content type. Declared by the page as <link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/themes/cdu_theme/favicon/apple-touch-icon.png" sizes="180x180">. Decoded and rendered: the Charles Darwin University shield crest - the Southern Cross star, the seven-petal CDU flower mark and the swoosh - drawn in CDU brand navy #211545 on an opaque white field. Dark navy artwork on opaque white with no conditional styling, so it is legible on a light card in every colour scheme.

notes: Same structural trap as Bond on this shard. CDU's real header lockup is an inline SVG with no src - twice on the page (sticky header and main header): - so per rule 5 there is no URL to report for it. I then took the site's own icon asset /themes/cdu_theme/favicon/icon.svg, which probes HTTP 200 image/svg+xml and is the same navy artwork, but rejected it: its embedded stylesheet is '.favicon { fill: #211545 } @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { .favicon { fill: #fff } }', so a visitor with a dark-mode OS gets a pure white crest that vanishes on a light card. An SVG loaded via resolves prefers-color-scheme against the reader's system, not the card, so that is a real rule 3 violation rather than a theoretical one. The apple-touch-icon.png carries the identical crest with no conditional CSS and an opaque background, so it is unconditionally safe. Rejected og:image (https://www.cdu.edu.au/files/styles/content_desktop_1x/public/2020-09/Group%201.jpg.webp?itok=8gug4bV7, alt 'scholarship') as programme photography rather than a mark. Provenance: CDU's own crest on cdu.edu.au for a CDU Vice-Chancellor's award, so rule 2 holds. This is a crest without the wordmark, which the brief allows in preference to a bare favicon glyph, and it is the best rule-3-safe option the site exposes at a URL.
